title: Reduce SLI metric cardinality for per-route/per-model breakdowns (aggregation + sampling)
author: Thomas Baird
description: Context: With tier-aware SLO dashboards we started slicing by tier/region/route/model. The combination of route (full path), model (fine-grained), customer (Dedicated), and result_code has pushed series counts well beyond our intended budget, causing elevated Prometheus remote_write queue pressure and expensive queries in Console dashboards. This PR reduces metrics cardinality while preserving what we need for tiered SLO + burn-rate alerting. Summary of changes: 1) Introduce canonical aggregation for route + model labels used by SLI metrics (gateway + routing + runtime). We replace high-cardinality labels (route, model_id) with bounded alternatives (route_group, model_family) for SLI-facing metrics. 2) Add sampling for high-volume endpoints where per-request series do not change SLO outcomes (embeddings and /v1/chat/completions streaming token events). Sampling is applied before export and preserves unbiased rates by emitting a sample_rate label + multiplier in the SLI query helpers. 3) Add a small allowlist/override mechanism so we can keep full fidelity labels for a limited set of endpoints during investigations (timeboxed; defaults off). 4) Update SLO queries in slo-toolkit-compatible format to consume route_group/model_family and sample-aware counters. Indicator impact: - Availability/error-rate SLIs remain based on request_total{status_class=...} counters; only labels change. - Latency SLIs (histograms) remain unsampled; we only aggregate route/model labels. - Streaming disconnect counters are aggregated to route_group and model_family, which matches the disconnect taxonomy work. Implementation details: - New mapping helpers in gateway metrics emitter: route -> route_group (e.g. /v1/chat/completions -> chat.completions, /v1/embeddings -> embeddings). Unknown paths map to "other" and are still tier/region-scoped. - model_id -> model_family: normalized by registry metadata (e.g. "llama-3.1-70b-instruct" -> "llama-3.1-70b", "qwen2.5-72b-instruct" -> "qwen2.5-72b"). For private/custom model IDs we map to "custom" unless model_family is explicitly set in config. - Sampling: embeddings request counters and streaming token event counters are sampled at default 1/20 when rps > threshold (configurable per service); emitted as redwood_api_requests_total_sampled with label sample_rate="0.05"; slo-toolkit query helper multiplies by (1/sample_rate) for rate calculations. - Dedicated: we do NOT include customer_id on SLI metrics by default; Dedicated per-customer views should be computed via separate, access-restricted metrics streams (follow-up). This PR ensures the default pipeline cannot accidentally explode due to customer label inclusion. Rollout plan: - Land behind feature flags: METRICS_CARDINALITY_REDUCE=off by default. - Enable in staging for 24h, validate series count + query parity dashboards. - Enable prod (Hosted first), then Dedicated. Links: - Linear: ENG-2424 - Related: ENG-2418/ENG-2420 (tiered SLIs + burn alerts), ENG-2425 (dashboards), ENG-2428 (streaming disconnect classification). Testing: unit tests for mapping + sampling; integration test validates we emit bounded label sets; load test on gateway metrics exporter shows ~68% reduction in active series for SLI metrics and ~45% reduction in remote_write bytes under peak replay. Release notes: No customer-facing changes; internal metrics label changes. Dashboards/alerts consuming old labels have been updated in observability-pack in a separate PR; do not enable the flag until dashboards are deployed.
commits: metrics: add route_group + model_family mappers for SLI emitters
gateway: sample embeddings + streaming token counters under high RPS
telemetry: add bounded-label enforcement + series budget warnings
slo: add sample-aware query helper + update default queries
tests: mapping, sampling determinism, and integration coverage
conversation: Logan Wright (reviewer): Big +1 on getting series count down. Two questions: (1) can we guarantee route_group is stable across gateway + routing + runtime? (2) sampling: are we sampling request counters only or also duration histograms?

Thomas Baird (author): (1) Yes—route_group is computed at the gateway and propagated via request context header x-rw-route-group; routing/runtime only re-emit the propagated value. If missing, they compute locally with the same mapping table (shared lib) but that should only happen for internal calls. (2) Sampling only applies to counters (requests_total + stream_token_events_total). Duration histograms are unsampled; only aggregated labels.

Nadia Rahman (reviewer): The sample_rate label looks like a potential cardinality footgun (float formatting). Please make it a small finite set (e.g. "1", "0.5", "0.1", "0.05"). Also add guardrails so it can’t become per-request.
Thomas Baird (author): Good catch. Updated sampler config to pick from an enum set and emit exact string constants. Also added validation in config parsing to reject arbitrary values.
Allison Grant (reviewer): Please document the new “bounded labels” contract. Also, can we add a metric/alert when the enforcer drops labels so we don’t silently lose fidelity?

Thomas Baird (author): Added docs/internal/observability/metric-labels.md section "SLI metrics bounded labels" + exported counter redwood_metrics_labels_dropped_total{reason=...}. We can template an alert in observability-pack (follow-up) but the counter is here.
Sergio Costa (reviewer): Dashboard queries will break if they still reference route/model_id. Are we coordinating the dashboard change? Also, do we keep both metrics for a deprecation window?

Thomas Baird (author): Coordinated with PR in observability-pack (Sergio’s PR). For this PR: we emit both label sets only when METRICS_CARDINALITY_REDUCE is off (legacy). When flag is on, old labels are not emitted on SLI metrics. Docs updated to require deploying dashboard updates before flipping the flag.
Caleb Johnson (reviewer): Concern: model_family mapping depends on registry metadata; what happens during catalog outages or when a new model ships without metadata? Also any perf impact on hot path?

Thomas Baird (author): Fallback path: if registry lookup fails, we map to "unknown" and increment redwood_model_family_lookup_fail_total. The mapping table is cached (TTL 10m) and hot path does not do network calls. Added benchmarks: overhead <1.5% on gateway emit path in our synthetic test.
Logan Wright (reviewer): Requested change: enforce that route_group is one of N known values (string set) to keep it bounded. Right now it looks like it can pass through arbitrary header values.
Thomas Baird (author): Added validation: if propagated route_group is not in allowlist, we coerce to "other" and count redwood_route_group_invalid_total. Tests added.
Sergio Costa (reviewer): Approved once CI is green.
merge_commit: a9c2d54c9d3e (squash): metrics: reduce SLI cardinality via aggregation + sampling
release_notes: Internal: SLI metrics now use bounded labels (route_group, model_family) and sample-aware counters for high-volume endpoints behind METRICS_CARDINALITY_REDUCE flag. Deploy dashboard/query updates before enabling flag in prod.
